clue.text: Rover a faithful friend put in reverse

indicators.note: put in reverse tells us the friend's name is read from back to front

parts.note: Damon, of the classical pair Damon and Pythias, is the byword for a faithful friend

explanation.surface: A dog owner backs their loyal pet, a rover, out of the drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in reverse' turns DAMON round to give the answer. Damon and Pythias were the legendary friends who would each die for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer with no fixed home, which is exactly what a nomad is: a synonym.

clue.text: Alternative to pyjamas, almost casual attire

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
a T-shirt is informal clothing

explanation.surface: Someone choosing bedwear settles on near-casual clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose shirt worn in bed is what people wear instead of pyjamas.

clue.text: In the mouths of many Americans, toupee is rug

definitions.text: In the mouths of many Americans, toupee

explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a toupee can be called this, and a small floor covering is one too.

clue.text: I had to go up to bank urgently

indicators.note: in a down clue, to go up is to be read from bottom to top

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A customer needed to get to the bank in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up' reverses ID to DI; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Direly means in a dreadful or desperate way, close in sense to urgently or desperately.

clue.text: Alternate opinions about performance

indicators.note: about tells us the opinions word goes round the performance word

parts.note: takes are opinions or points of view
a turn is a short stage act or performance

explanation.surface: Reviewers swap views on a show, each giving their verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, and 'about' is the container signal rather than 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to do something one after another in rotation, which is what people do when they take turns.

clue.text: Pole — her turn to move

indicators.note: move tells us the letters of the words before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: In a game it is now her turn to make a move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges HER TURN TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The direction of the geographic North Pole, as opposed to magnetic north, is a pole: a synonym by reference.

clue.text: Thus nobleman shortly rises, to acclaim

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: so means thus or in this way

indicators.note: shortly means the nobleman's word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a duke is a high-ranking nobleman

explanation.surface: A peer stands briefly to receive applause.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' reads the whole joined piece upwards; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise or honour received for an achievement, so it is a synonym of acclaim.

clue.text: Description of race to shower that's working

indicators.note: working means the letters are being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Athletes run a race to get to the showers that still function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges TO SHOWER; 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest between only two serious contenders is called this, from a race with just two runners.

clue.text: Waves may make trouble

definitions.meaning: big waves can toss a small craft from side to side
to stir up difficulty or upset a settled situation

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, waves set a small vessel swaying; as an idiom, it means to disturb things and cause trouble.

clue.text: Measure stride

definitions.meaning: an action taken towards a goal, as in taking measures
a single pace made in walking

explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an action taken, as in steps to fix a problem; a stride is a pace in walking.

clue.text: Travel to find some golf

parts.note: to get something is to find or obtain it
a round is a single game of golf, a bit of golf

explanation.surface: A keen golfer goes on holiday to squeeze in a few holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To get around is an idiom for travelling widely or moving from place to place.

clue.text: At the right moment you can find chalk here

definitions.meaning: exactly when expected, like an actor coming in at the signal
snooker players chalk the tip of the stick they strike with, so chalk sits on that stick

explanation.definitionFit: Coming in at the signal means arriving exactly at the right moment; snooker chalk goes on the tip of the stick.

clue.text: Seek a quarrel, disrupting a rotten social

indicators.note: disrupting means the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone spoils for a fight and wrecks a dismal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupting' rearranges the thirteen letters of A ROTTEN SOCIAL. The idiom comes from trailing your coat on the ground and daring someone to tread on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to provoke deliberately, inviting a fight, so it means seeking a quarrel.

clue.text: Bit (it's a coin) exchanged for drugs

indicators.note: exchanged means the letters are swapped around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with it's giving its three letters

explanation.surface: A small coin is traded in return for medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' rearranges the eleven letters of BIT ITS A COIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria, a particular class of drugs.

clue.text: Top pick TV awards up, use a ploy almost crooked

parts.note: A is the top grade, the first choice

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the awards word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Emmys are American television awards

indicators.note: almost means the ploy word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trick is a ploy or ruse

explanation.surface: To win TV prizes, a contestant uses a slightly dishonest trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EMMYS to SYMME; 'almost' trims TRICK to TRIC. 'use a' is linking text.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetric means lopsided or uneven, so it can mean crooked in the sense of not straight.

clue.text: Emotion has husband worried

parts.note: something that worried you ate at you, so ate means worried

explanation.surface: A wife notes that her husband is anxious and full of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is a strong feeling, so it is one example of an emotion.

clue.text: Bias shown by reporters about law enforcers

indicators.note: about tells us the reporters word goes round the law enforcers word

parts.note: the press are reporters collectively
a posse is a band of men gathered by a sheriff to enforce the law

explanation.surface: Journalists show prejudice in their coverage of the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bias' is the verb here, to influence in advance, and 'shown by' only joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepossess is to prejudice or influence someone beforehand, so it is a synonym of the verb to bias.

clue.text: Those who opposed Indians putting up tearoom surrounded by fencing

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us the tearoom word sits inside the fencing word

parts.note: pales are the stakes of a fence, so fencing

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means reading the tearoom word upwards

parts.note: a cafe is a tearoom

explanation.surface: Settlers build a tearoom within a fenced compound to defy local tribes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the old Western-film usage: settlers whom Native Americans fought, seen from the tribes' side.
explanation.definitionFit: In Western films this was the name Native Americans used for the white settlers they fought.

clue.text: Suffering bad birth in small pool

indicators.note: suffering tells us the words that follow are to be battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman endures a difficult delivery in a birthing pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' rearranges BAD BIRTH; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow basin of water for birds to bathe in is a very small pool.

clue.text: Teacher has to stand in some places visited by Alice

definitions.note: the clue's plural is loose: the answer is one of the places Alice goes

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
thole is an old and Scottish word meaning to endure or stand

explanation.surface: A tutor must stand in for others at several places Alice visited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'in some' are link words. Alice falls down a rabbit hole at the start of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's story Alice follows the White Rabbit down its burrow into Wonderland: the literary reference.

clue.text: Seat in class

definitions.meaning: a hare's lair or resting place in the grass is called by this name
a school year group in British schools, such as the sixth

explanation.definitionFit: A hare's seat is its form, and a school class is a form in Britain.

clue.text: Some of a brickie's handiwork?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bricklayer's work is admired in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: the fabric of a building is what a bricklayer makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric of a building is its walls and structure, which is a builder's handiwork.

clue.text: "Fire at will', for instance, where troops are deployed

definitions.meaning: a command given in a fight, an example of an instruction in combat
the arrangement and disposition of military units for a fight

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is read literally as a command issued in a fight, and in military language it means the disposition of forces.

clue.text: Jockey's condition

definitions.meaning: someone who rides a horse in a race
a clause added to a contract or bill that sets terms

explanation.definitionFit: A jockey rides horses; an added clause setting terms is also called this, a condition.

clue.text: Arrange for doctor to join firm

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A GP is asked to arrange to join a practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'to join' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb is to tidy or arrange hair by drawing teeth through it.

clue.text: Board getting agreement from both France and Germany

parts.words: agreement from both France and Germany
parts.note: oui is French for yes

parts.words: agreement from both France and Germany
parts.note: ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A deal on a governing board wins approval from Paris and Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: The board's trade name is made of the French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lettered board used at seances for supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Artisan is a number of days ahead of speaker

indicators.note: ahead of places the days piece in front of the speaker

parts.note: Dec is short for December, a month and so a number of days
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A craftsman arrives some days before the lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and decorator is a skilled tradesman, which is what an artisan is.

clue.text: Test set up for famous schoolboy

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars

explanation.surface: An examination is arranged for a well-known pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns MOT round. The MOT is Britain's yearly safety test for cars; Tom Brown's Schooldays is a Victorian school story.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Brown, hero of Thomas Hughes's novel of Rugby School, is literature's best-known schoolboy.

clue.text: Stretch of water provided by employer and adapted to our use, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that we are to hear the words spoken rather than read

parts.words: employer and adapted to our use
parts.note: an employer is a boss, and something adapted to our use is for us

explanation.surface: A firm's chief provides a waterway made fit for the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided by' is a link word. Said out loud, BOSS FOR US gives the strait at Istanbul.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bosphorus is the strait linking the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara: a named example.

clue.text: Pear detailed in magazine

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed: the last letter of the pear is cut off

parts.note: the Comice is a variety of pear

explanation.surface: A pear is described in detail in a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' takes the last letter off COMICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a children's magazine of strip cartoons, so it is a kind of magazine.
